exprVars.renameHint: Letters, digits and underscore only (no CJK, spaces or dashes) — the runtime turns variable names into function parameter names, so a non-ASCII name simply cannot be read inside the expression. Renaming also updates the edges connected to it and the old name inside the expression.

renameError.notIdentifier: Use letters, digits and underscore only, and do not start with a digit (CJK, spaces or dashes cannot be read inside an expression)
renameError.reserved: This is a JS reserved word; using it as a variable name makes the whole expression fail to evaluate (try something like myClass)
renameError.unsafe: The evaluator uses this name, or it would shadow a global (undefined / NaN / Infinity / __in) — pick another
renameError.forbidden: This name has a special meaning (it would change the object prototype) — pick another
renameError.taken: A variable or port with this name already exists — one of them would silently overwrite the other and the value would be wrong
renameError.configKey: This name is taken by the node’s own config (mode/expression/formulas…), so it cannot be read inside the expression

code.nodeGuide: How to write a custom node
code.nodeGuideTitle: How to write a custom node (full guide)
code.nodeGuideIntro: There are **two ways** to add a new capability to your bot, in this order: ① **Compose** (no code) — if existing nodes can do it, just wire them; when the same logic is used 2+ times and you want one edit to change all of them, make it a **subflow** (canvas: "Subflow definition" + "Call subflow"). ② **Write code** (this page) — only when the canvas truly cannot express it (external APIs, complex computation). This page covers ②: copy the sample node package into the project's plugins/ folder and it takes effect without restarting; errors surface at load time, not at runtime.
code.newNodeTitle: New custom node (creates an editable skeleton under plugins/)
code.newNodeIntro: Creates plugins/<name>/manifest.json and index.js in your project and opens index.js for editing. Saving takes effect immediately - no restart. An existing directory is refused; your code is never overwritten.

endNode.empty: No return values yet — click “+ Add return value” below to start
endNode.fieldRequired: Each item must have a string `field`
endNode.plainNote: The end node of a normal flow. Code after this node does not run; no return values to configure.
endNode.subflowNote: Define the subflow return values. `field` is the key in the returned dict; `source` is picked from upstream node outputs.

ifBranch.complexNote: This expression is too complex for visual editing. Switch to advanced mode to edit it directly.
ifBranch.noConditions: No conditions yet — add one below
ifBranch.title: Condition builder
ifBranch.visualHintPrefix: Visual mode suits simple conditions (with AND/OR). For complex expressions (function calls, arithmetic) switch to advanced mode, or use the

inlineCommand.emptyRow: No tags in this row yet
inlineCommand.enterGroupWarning: "Send immediately on tap" is officially **unsupported in group chats and text channels** — in a group it will not render as a tappable tag. Use "Fill the input box on tap" for groups.
inlineCommand.hint: A piece of **tappable text inside the body** (officially a "command-input"). A tap **fills the command into the input box** and the user presses send. Unlike buttons it lives in the body text and does not consume the 5-row button budget.
inlineCommand.modeInput: Fill the input box on tap

keyboard.actionHint: What happens on click: open link = open the URL; callback to bot = send data to the bot (listen with a button_clicked node); send command = post the command text **as the user**, as if they had typed it (triggers message_received)
keyboard.jsonHint: Edits to the JSON are synced to the visual editor and the preview automatically
keyboard.permHint: Who can click: specific user = only that QQ account; admins only = group owner/admins; everyone = anyone; specific role = members with that role
keyboard.previewLabel: QQ preview (click a button to simulate a click)
keyboard.styleHint: Button style: grey outline = secondary action (subtle), blue outline = primary action (more prominent, invites clicks)

messageAction.newPanelHint: Type a panel name and press Enter to confirm
messageAction.newPanelTitle: Create a new panel and apply it to this node
messageAction.noPanelRef: — Do not reference a panel (edit inline) —
messageAction.panelRefNote: This node references a panel. After editing the panel, click “Sync” to update this node's button config.
messageAction.saveBackTitle: Save this node's button config back to the global panel
messageAction.syncTitle: Re-sync the button config from the global panel to this node

shortcuts.connectDesc: Connect two nodes (drag from the ● on the right to the next node)
shortcuts.escDesc: Clear selection / close the config panel
shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts

startNode.intervalLabel: Interval in seconds (takes precedence over cron when > 0)
startNode.noticeNote: Triggers on group notices (pokes, recalls, etc.). No extra configuration needed.
startNode.requestNote: Triggers when a friend request or group join request arrives. No extra configuration needed.

subflowParams.nameRequired: Each item must have a string `name`
subflowParams.note: Define the subflow inputs. The caller passes them through the args port, and the subflow body can reference each parameter by name.

switchCase.defaultHint: Taken when no case matches — like the default branch of a switch statement
switchCase.empty: No cases yet — click “+ Add case” below to start
switchCase.labelMatchRequired: Each item must have string `label` and `match` fields

tablePicker.clickToInsert: 💡 Click a field name to insert it into the current input
tablePicker.loadSchemaFailed: Failed to load the table schema: {error}
tablePicker.selectTableHint: ← Pick a table on the left to see its fields
tablePicker.title: Table structure browser

bot.restartCancelledNotSaved: The flow was not saved, so the restart was cancelled (check .qqbat/flow.json)
bot.startCancelledNotSaved: The flow was not saved, so the start was cancelled (check .qqbat/flow.json)

flatten.multipleConsumers: The template output is used in {count} places (exactly 1 required)
flatten.namedVars: Uses named variables (variables_json); flattening would lose them
flatten.notSendNode: The downstream node is not a “Send message” node
flatten.notTextPort: The downstream port is “{port}”, not a text port
flatten.portMissing: The template port “{port}” does not exist on “Send message”
flatten.portOccupied: The “{port}” port on “Send message” is already taken by another edge
flatten.textOccupied: The downstream “Send message” node already has content
flatten.tooManyVars: The template uses {vars}, but “Send message” only supports var1~var4
flatten.wrongMode: The downstream “Send message” node is not in “{mode}” mode

autoGroup.onlyTrigger: The chain has only the trigger and nothing else
autoGroup.duplicate: A group with the same nodes already exists ("{title}")
autoGroup.overlapExisting: Nodes are already in group "{group}" (groups may not overlap)
autoGroup.overlapPlanned: Shares nodes with an earlier chain (groups may not overlap)

checkExists.description: Check whether a key exists and branch on it with branch_if
checkExists.name: Check whether data exists
checkExists.usageHint: Wire the exists result to branch_if.value: the true branch means it exists, the false branch means it does not

combatRound.description: Read HP → subtract damage → save the new HP → reply
combatRound.name: Combat round
combatRound.usageHint: Read HP (v1, defaults to 100 when the key is missing) → subtract a fixed 8 damage → save the new HP → format → reply. For real damage, replace the 8 in the expression with a value wired from an upstream node into expression_eval.v2

contextReply.description: Get the user's QQ number, format it and reply
contextReply.name: Get context and reply
contextReply.usageHint: get_ids extracts the QQ number → format_text formats it → message_send replies. var1 is bound to the QQ number

cooldownCheck.description: Read the cooldown flag → true when free, false while cooling down
cooldownCheck.name: Cooldown check
cooldownCheck.usageHint: Read the cooldown value and branch: !value = true (not cooling down) takes the true branch and replies “success”; the false branch replies “cooling down”. Replace the true-branch message_send with your real logic

cultivate.description: Read exp → +10 → save the new exp → reply with the current exp
cultivate.name: Cultivate
cultivate.usageHint: Read exp → +10 → save the new exp → format → reply. It always saves and replies; add branch_if(value >= 100) yourself if you want a level-up message

delayExecution.description: Wait 3 seconds before continuing to the next node
delayExecution.name: Delayed execution
delayExecution.usageHint: Single-node snippet. Continues after a 3-second delay — useful for throttling, typing simulation or delayed replies

formatAndReply.description: Build text from a template and reply automatically
formatAndReply.name: Format and reply
formatAndReply.usageHint: format_text formats the text and feeds message_send.text to reply automatically. A built-in {name} value is provided (editable in the variables_json field of the property panel); you can also wire a value in from an upstream node

gachaPull.description: Weighted random → save the result → format → reply
gachaPull.name: Gacha pull
gachaPull.usageHint: Weighted random (SSR/SR/R at 1:9:90) → save the result → format → reply. It always saves and replies; add branch_if(value == "ssr") yourself for a special SSR message

incrementCounter.description: Atomically increment a numeric persistent variable (e.g. login count)
incrementCounter.name: Increment counter
incrementCounter.usageHint: Single-node snippet. Increments login_count and outputs the new value on the result port

inventoryAdd.description: Read inventory → append the new item → save → notify
inventoryAdd.name: Add item
inventoryAdd.usageHint: Read the inventory list → list_op(append) appends the element → save the new list → format the notice → reply. Bind the item to add through the list_op.item port; {var1} is the new list (shown as JSON — use expression_eval to compute its length instead)

inventoryView.description: Read the player's inventory and format it for display
inventoryView.name: View inventory
inventoryView.usageHint: Read the inventory persistent variable → format it as an inventory list → reply. Store inventory data as a list or dict

leaderboard.description: Read the score list → sort → format → reply
leaderboard.name: Leaderboard
leaderboard.usageHint: Read the global scores list → list_op(sort) sorts it → format it as leaderboard text → reply. Store scores as a numeric list so the sorted output can be shown directly

pkAttack.description: Read attack power → compute damage → save → reply
pkAttack.name: PK attack
pkAttack.usageHint: Read player_atk (v1, defaults to 50 when the key is missing) → compute atk*1.5 → save the damage → format → reply. For real damage, change the expression to v1*1.5-v2 and wire v2 in from upstream

questAccept.description: Check the player level → save the quest when eligible → reply success or level too low
questAccept.name: Accept a quest
questAccept.usageHint: Level ≥ 5 takes the true branch: save active_quest → reply success; the false branch replies “level too low”. Bind the quest ID/name through the second variable_persist.value port (e.g. from the on_command args)

randomReply.description: Pick one message at random from a list and reply with it
randomReply.name: Random reply
randomReply.usageHint: random(choice) picks one reply at random from the list (three candidates are built in; edit them in the items field of the property panel). The list is a JSON array

readPlayerData.description: Read player data from persistent storage (user scope)
readPlayerData.name: Read player data
readPlayerData.usageHint: Single-node snippet. Once wired after a trigger, it outputs the player data on the result port

savePlayerData.description: Save data to persistent storage (user scope)
savePlayerData.name: Save player data
savePlayerData.usageHint: Single-node snippet. Pass the data to save through the value port

shopBuy.description: Read gold → check whether it is enough → deduct and save, or warn
shopBuy.name: Buy an item
shopBuy.usageHint: Gold ≥ 100 takes the true branch: deduct 100 → save → reply with the remaining gold; the false branch replies “not enough gold”. Edit the expression and the branch_if condition to change the price

signinFlow.description: Check check-in status → if not yet checked in, read exp and add 10 → save → reply
signinFlow.name: Daily check-in flow
signinFlow.usageHint: When not yet checked in, the true branch runs: read exp → +10 → save the new exp → reply. Add your own “already checked in” message to the false branch

timeFormat.description: Get the current time and output it as %Y-%m-%d %H:%M
timeFormat.name: Format time
timeFormat.usageHint: Single-node snippet. time_op(now) already formats via fmt and outputs a "2026-07-10 14:30" style string on the datetime port. Change fmt to adjust the format

tryCatchBlock.description: Wrap error handling with try_catch: try for the happy path, catch for errors, finally for cleanup
tryCatchBlock.name: Exception handling
tryCatchBlock.usageHint: Single-node snippet. Wire normal logic to the try port, error handling to catch, and cleanup to finally

validation.controlLoop: May create a control-flow loop (risk of infinite execution)
validation.controlLoopHint: Check the logic: A→B→...→A causes infinite execution
validation.dataTypeMismatchHint: Add a type-conversion node, or check the upstream node output type (current: {source}, required: {target})
validation.missingRequiredInput: Required data port "{name}" has no data source
validation.missingRequiredInputHint: Drag a data edge from an upstream node to this port, or bind a default value in the property panel
validation.portKindHint: Control ports can only connect to control ports, data ports to data ports
validation.sameNode: A node cannot connect to itself
validation.triggerAsTarget: A trigger is the entry point of a flow and cannot be a downstream node
validation.triggerAsTargetHint: Use the trigger as the starting point and connect it to an action/logic node
validation.modeForwardRequired: Forward mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.modeKeyboardButtonsRequired: Button-UI mode requires 「{field}」 (at least one row)
validation.modeKeyboardRequired: Button-UI mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.modeMarkdownRequired: Markdown mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.modeMediaRequired: Rich-media mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.modeSegmentRequired: Message-segment mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.modeStreamPrivateOnly: Streaming messages are single-chat only — change 「{field}」 to a private push
validation.modeStreamRequired: Streaming mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.modeTextRequired: Plain-text mode requires 「{field}」 or an upstream binding
validation.proactiveTargetRequired: Fill in 「{field}」 or bind upstream data when pushing proactively

flow.subflowInUse: This subflow definition is referenced by 「{names}」 — delete or unbind those call nodes first

reason.actionAfterBranch: Run an action after the branch
reason.actionInLoop: Run an action inside the loop

agent.followGlobalHint: Clear this project’s own config and use the global one

field.baseUrlHint: Leave empty for the provider default

global.title: Global agent
global.subtitle: For development, shared by every project

projects.title: Bot projects
projects.subtitle: Each project’s own AI chat (follows global by default)

agent.devAssistantHint: Two sections, two jobs: Global agent is the developer assistant you use inside the app (writes flows, generates code; shared by every project). Bot projects is the model your bot uses when talking to people (follows the global config by default).
agent.testNeedRestart: The test was not sent — the new channel only takes effect after an app restart (the renderer hot-reloads, the main process/preload do not)
